literature.headline_zh: 麻疹病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期麻疹病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 2025年1月至2026年4月,美国确诊了4102例麻疹病例,其中92.5%的病例未接种疫苗或疫苗接种状态未知;23.7%的病例为5岁以下儿童,47.4%为5-19岁儿童。 [10.1111/josh.70202]

对 77 名患者的分析表明,超过 2 年的生存期是可以实现的,但存在差异。生存分布显示,44.2% 的生存时间为 2 至 <5 年,28.6% 的生存时间为 5 至 <10 年,27.3% 的生存时间≥10 年。尽管 62.3% 的患者最初获得缓解或稳定,但 31.2% 的患者后来出现病情进展、严重残疾或死亡。报告的与延长生存期相关的因素包括 治疗 反应性 (62.3%)、疾病进展缓慢 (24.7%) 和复发缓解或双相模式 (20.8%)。其他影响因素包括 宿主 相关因素 (18.2%)、成人发病疾病 (10.4%)、早期 诊断 和脑电图改善。在 31 项 队列研究 研究中,总生存率仍然很低。 [10.47936/encephalitis.2026.00108]
大多数 麻疹 患者是 患病率 合并症和并发症较高的婴儿,并且大量患者的 疫苗接种 覆盖范围不足。系统发育分析揭示了与俄罗斯和美国流行的 B3 菌株的相关性,强调了全球传播。氨基酸取代和结构分析强调了当前分离株与参考菌株相比的微小结构变化。 [10.1016/j.compbiomed.2026.111757]
医护人员中74.9%的血清流行率免疫阳性,25.1%不阳性,均报告过疫苗接种,年龄与IgG水平和免疫状态呈显着正相关,年龄每增加一岁,免疫阳性的几率增加14.3%,与性别无显着相关。 [10.1111/tmi.70207]
该综述确定了与 麻疹 感染相关的一致血液学异常,包括淋巴细胞减少和血小板减少,作为回顾性临床数据支持的关键发现。这些变化被强调为急性 麻疹 发作期间的典型实验室特征。 [10.1111/ijlh.70213]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: From January 2025 to April 2026, there were 4,102 diagnosed measles cases in the United States, with 92.5% of cases being unvaccinated or having unknown vaccination status; 23.7% of cases were in children under 5 years, and 47.4% in those aged 5–19. [10.1111/josh.70202]

The estimated number susceptible in Israel on 1 March 2018 ranged from 0.55 million (6.3%) to 1.92 million (22.4%), with a central estimate of 1.22 million (14.2%). Children aged <1 year had the highest central susceptible proportion (75.7%) and incidence (196.0 per 100,000). [10.64898/2026.07.28.26359095]

Analysis of 77 patients demonstrated that survival beyond 2 years is achievable but variable. Survival distribution showed 44.2% surviving 2 to <5 years, 28.6% surviving 5 to <10 years, and 27.3% surviving ≥10 years. [10.47936/encephalitis.2026.00108]

Most of the measles patients were infants with a high prevalence of comorbidity and complications, and significant number of patients had inadequate vaccination coverage. The phylogenetic analysis revealed relatedness to B3 strains circulating in Russia and the USA, emphasizing the global spread. [10.1016/j.compbiomed.2026.111757]

74.9% seroprevalence of positive immunity among HCWs, 25.1% not positive, all reported prior vaccination, age showed significant positive correlation with IgG levels and immunity status, each additional year of age increased odds of positive immunity by 14.3%, no significant association with sex. [10.1111/tmi.70207]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期麻疹病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
2025年1月至2026年4月,美国确诊了4102例麻疹病例,其中92.5%的病例未接种疫苗或疫苗接种状态未知;23.7%的病例为5岁以下儿童,47.4%为5-19岁儿童。 [10.1111/josh.70202]。

对 77 名患者的分析表明,超过 2 年的生存期是可以实现的,但存在差异。生存分布显示,44.2% 的生存时间为 2 至 <5 年,28.6% 的生存时间为 5 至 <10 年,27.3% 的生存时间≥10 年。尽管 62.3% 的患者最初获得缓解或稳定,但 31.2% 的患者后来出现病情进展、严重残疾或死亡。报告的与延长生存期相关的因素包括 治疗 反应性 (62.3%)、疾病进展缓慢 (24.7%) 和复发缓解或双相模式 (20.8%)。其他影响因素包括 宿主 相关因素 (18.2%)、成人发病疾病 (10.4%)、早期 诊断 和脑电图改善。在 31 项 队列研究 研究中,总生存率仍然很低。
大多数 麻疹 患者是 患病率 合并症和并发症较高的婴儿,并且大量患者的 疫苗接种 覆盖范围不足。系统发育分析揭示了与俄罗斯和美国流行的 B3 菌株的相关性,强调了全球传播。氨基酸取代和结构分析强调了当前分离株与参考菌株相比的微小结构变化。
医护人员中74.9%的血清流行率免疫阳性,25.1%不阳性,均报告过疫苗接种,年龄与IgG水平和免疫状态呈显着正相关,年龄每增加一岁,免疫阳性的几率增加14.3%,与性别无显着相关。 [10.1111/tmi.70207]。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

From January 2025 to April 2026, there were 4,102 diagnosed measles cases in the United States, with 92.5% of cases being unvaccinated or having unknown vaccination status; 23.7% of cases were in children under 5 years, and 47.4% in those aged 5–19.
The estimated number susceptible in Israel on 1 March 2018 ranged from 0.55 million (6.3%) to 1.92 million (22.4%), with a central estimate of 1.22 million (14.2%).

Analysis of 77 patients demonstrated that survival beyond 2 years is achievable but variable. Survival distribution showed 44.2% surviving 2 to <5 years, 28.6% surviving 5 to <10 years, and 27.3% surviving ≥10 years.
Most of the measles patients were infants with a high prevalence of comorbidity and complications, and significant number of patients had inadequate vaccination coverage.

papers.title: Long-term survival (≥2 years) in subacute sclerosing panencephalitis: a systematic review of prolonged survivors.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive and often fatal disorder with highly variable survival. This systematic review aimed to characterize long-term survival (≥2 years), remission, and stabilization, and identify determinants of favorable outcomes. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies including confirmed SSPE cases were considered eligible for inclusion. Individual patient analysis was restricted to cases with ≥2 years of follow-up. Data were extracted at the patient and cohort levels. RESULTS: Analysis of 77 patients demonstrated that survival beyond 2 years is achievable but variable. Survival distribution showed 44.2% surviving 2 to <5 years, 28.6% surviving 5 to <10 years, and 27.3% surviving ≥10 years. Although 62.3% initially achieved remission or stabilization, 31.2% later developed progression, severe disability, or death. Reported factors associated with prolonged survival included treatment responsiveness (62.3%), slow disease progression (24.7%), and relapsing-remitting or biphasic patterns (20.8%). Additional contributors were host-related factors (18.2%), adult-onset disease (10.4%), early diagnosis, and electroencephalographic improvement. Across 31 cohort studies, overall survival remained poor. Survival beyond 2 years was inconsistently reported and varied widely. Remission or stabilization was observed in some studies, but disease progression remained the predominant outcome. Mortality ranged from low to very high across cohorts. Reported factors associated with improved survival included slower disease progression, older age at onset, earlier stage at diagnosis, and use of therapies such as inosine pranobex and interferon. CONCLUSION: SSPE survival outcomes show marked heterogeneity. Although prolonged survival occurs in some, most patients have poor outcomes, emphasizing the importance of early diagnosis and the need for effective therapies.

papers.source_body_en: PURPOSE: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a progressive and often fatal disorder with highly variable survival. This systematic review aimed to characterize long-term survival (≥2 years), remission, and stabilization, and identify determinants of favorable outcomes. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies including confirmed SSPE cases were considered eligible for inclusion. Individual patient analysis was restricted to cases with ≥2 years of follow-up. Data were extracted at the patient and cohort levels. RESULTS: Analysis of 77 patients demonstrated that survival beyond 2 years is achievable but variable. Survival distribution showed 44.2% surviving 2 to <5 years, 28.6% surviving 5 to <10 years, and 27.3% surviving ≥10 years. Although 62.3% initially achieved remission or stabilization, 31.2% later developed progression, severe disability, or death. Reported factors associated with prolonged survival included treatment responsiveness (62.3%), slow disease progression (24.7%), and relapsing-remitting or biphasic patterns (20.8%). Additional contributors were host-related factors (18.2%), adult-onset disease (10.4%), early diagnosis, and electroencephalographic improvement. Across 31 cohort studies, overall survival remained poor. Survival beyond 2 years was inconsistently reported and varied widely. Remission or stabilization was observed in some studies, but disease progression remained the predominant outcome. Mortality ranged from low to very high across cohorts. Reported factors associated with improved survival included slower disease progression, older age at onset, earlier stage at diagnosis, and use of therapies such as inosine pranobex and interferon. CONCLUSION: SSPE survival outcomes show marked heterogeneity. Although prolonged survival occurs in some, most patients have poor outcomes, emphasizing the importance of early diagnosis and the need for effective therapies.

papers.title: Measles Immunity and Associated Factors Among Healthcare Workers in Bandar Abbas Following the 2025 Outbreak: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Measles is a highly contagious viral infection that poses significant risks to healthcare workers (HCWs) during outbreaks and can lead to nosocomial transmission. Despite vaccination programmes, immunity gaps persist, as seen in the 2025 Bandar Abbas, Iran, outbreak, necessitating seroprevalence assessments among HCWs in vulnerable regions. To assess measles immunity seroprevalence among Bandar Abbas HCWs following the 2025 outbreak and examine associated demographic factors (age, sex). METHODS: This cross-sectional study surveyed 175 HCWs from three hospitals in Bandar Abbas using convenience sampling (January-April 2025). Data included questionnaires on demographics and vaccination, as well as ELISA-based serological IgG testing. Immunity was categorised as positive or not positive (negative/equivocal). Analyses employed Spearman's correlation, the Mann-Whitney U test, the Chi-square test and logistic regression (p < 0.05). RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 31.54 ± 7.42 years, and 62.9% were female. All reported prior measles vaccination. Seroprevalence of positive immunity was 74.9%, while 25.1% were not positive. Age showed a significant positive correlation with IgG levels (rho = 0.360, p < 0.001) and with immunity status (U = 1763.500, p < 0.001). Logistic regression revealed that each additional year of age increased the odds of positive immunity by 14.3% (OR = 1.143, 95% CI 1.061-1.232, p < 0.001). There was no significant association with sex (p = 0.813). Vaccination history could not be analysed due to insufficient variation. CONCLUSION: Notable immunity gaps in Bandar Abbas HCWs, especially among younger staff, underscore the need for targeted screening, boosters and enhanced infection control measures.

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 由于变异不足、便利抽样的潜在选择偏差、阿巴斯港卫生工作者之外的普遍性有限、未检查的其他人口因素的可能影响,无法分析 疫苗接种 历史。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要有针对性的筛查计划、加强 疫苗接种 策略、加强感染控制措施(特别是针对年轻医护人员)、进一步研究以调查 疫苗接种 历史影响和其他相关因素。

papers.title: From Seroprevalence to Measles Outbreak Risk: A Multicountry Epidemiological Proof of Concept
papers.abstract: Background: High national vaccination coverage may conceal age-specific and spatially concentrated measles susceptibility. Objective: To assess whether published age-specific seropositivity results can be converted into a time-updated susceptibility profile that corresponds with subsequent measles incidence, while distinguishing susceptibility from infectious introductions and transmission conditions. Methods: For Israel, published 2015 age-specific seropositivity estimates were mapped to monthly birth cohorts and projected to 1 March 2018, accounting for births, aging, maternal antibody, routine vaccination, vaccine effectiveness, and uncertainty in assay interpretation. The primary outcome was reported age-specific incidence during the 2018-2019 outbreak; national and Jerusalem District case burdens were secondary outcomes. Published evidence from the Netherlands, Czechia, and Australia was compared using a common framework covering age distribution, assay classification, vaccination, importation, spatial concentration, and transmission context. Results: The estimated number susceptible in Israel on 1 March 2018 ranged from approximately 0.55 million (6.3% of the modelled population) to 1.92 million (22.4%), with a central estimate of 1.22 million (14.2%). Children aged <1 year had the highest central susceptible proportion (75.7%) and the highest later incidence (196.0 per 100,000). Jerusalem District accounted for 2,202 of 4,311 reported national cases, consistent with susceptibility concentrated in communities with lower first-dose coverage. The external comparisons showed that clustering amplified Dutch outbreak risk, survey design affected Czech estimates, and importation dominated Australian activity. Conclusions: Published seropositivity can identify immunity gaps, but useful outbreak-risk assessment must also represent susceptible density and distribution, introduction pressure, and local transmission conditions. Although the model was not designed to compare alternative vaccination schedules directly, its identification of substantial susceptibility during early childhood provides epidemiological support for Israel's recent decision to advance the second routine MMRV dose from 6 years to 18 months of age, thereby shortening the period during which young children remain dependent on single-dose protection.

analysis.summary_en: This multicountry study developed a method to convert seroprevalence data into time-updated measles susceptibility profiles, validated against the 2018-2019 Israeli outbreak. The model estimated 0.55-1.92 million susceptible individuals in Israel (6.3-22.4%), with highest risk in infants (<1 year, 75.7% susceptible, 196/100,000 incidence). Jerusalem District accounted for 51% of cases, reflecting spatial clustering in low-coverage communities. External comparisons showed outbreak risk amplification in the Netherlands due to clustering, survey design effects in Czechia, and importation dominance in Australia. The approach identified early childhood susceptibility gaps, supporting Israel's policy to advance the second MMRV dose from 6 years to 18 months. The study demonstrates that seroprevalence data, when combined with demographic and vaccination dynamics, can predict outbreak risk and guide targeted interventions, though accuracy depends on local transmission conditions and data quality.

papers.title_zh: 从 血清流行率 到 麻疹 暴发 风险:多国流行病学概念证明
papers.source_body_en: Background: High national vaccination coverage may conceal age-specific and spatially concentrated measles susceptibility. Objective: To assess whether published age-specific seropositivity results can be converted into a time-updated susceptibility profile that corresponds with subsequent measles incidence, while distinguishing susceptibility from infectious introductions and transmission conditions. Methods: For Israel, published 2015 age-specific seropositivity estimates were mapped to monthly birth cohorts and projected to 1 March 2018, accounting for births, aging, maternal antibody, routine vaccination, vaccine effectiveness, and uncertainty in assay interpretation. The primary outcome was reported age-specific incidence during the 2018-2019 outbreak; national and Jerusalem District case burdens were secondary outcomes. Published evidence from the Netherlands, Czechia, and Australia was compared using a common framework covering age distribution, assay classification, vaccination, importation, spatial concentration, and transmission context. Results: The estimated number susceptible in Israel on 1 March 2018 ranged from approximately 0.55 million (6.3% of the modelled population) to 1.92 million (22.4%), with a central estimate of 1.22 million (14.2%). Children aged <1 year had the highest central susceptible proportion (75.7%) and the highest later incidence (196.0 per 100,000). Jerusalem District accounted for 2,202 of 4,311 reported national cases, consistent with susceptibility concentrated in communities with lower first-dose coverage. The external comparisons showed that clustering amplified Dutch outbreak risk, survey design affected Czech estimates, and importation dominated Australian activity. Conclusions: Published seropositivity can identify immunity gaps, but useful outbreak-risk assessment must also represent susceptible density and distribution, introduction pressure, and local transmission conditions. Although the model was not designed to compare alternative vaccination schedules directly, its identification of substantial susceptibility during early childhood provides epidemiological support for Israel's recent decision to advance the second routine MMRV dose from 6 years to 18 months of age, thereby shortening the period during which young children remain dependent on single-dose protection.

papers.full_text: Measles, one of the most contagious pathogens known, was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, yet it has re‐emerged as a growing epidemic threat. Schools now sit at the epicenter of this resurgence. Declining childhood vaccination rates, politicization of immunization policy, and erosion of institutional authority have converged to create conditions where measles can again spread through classrooms and communities. While cases were first reported in Texas in January 2025, from then through April 2026, there have been 4102 diagnosed cases of measles in the United States, where 92.5% were either unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status. Of these, 972 (23.7%) were among children younger than 5 years of age and 1944 (47.4%) in those ages 5–19 [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Federal policy shifts have intensified this epidemic. As Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has attempted to reshape national vaccine policy, including reducing the number of routinely recommended childhood vaccines and restructuring the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) [6]. Multiple federal courts have intervened. On March 16, 2026, United States District Judge Brian Murphy blocked key components of the overhaul, ruling that HHS had acted unlawfully and that the proposed changes would “reduce vaccination rates and harm public health.” [7] The efforts to revise the childhood vaccine schedule were ruled as arbitrary, capricious, and unsupported by scientific evidence [7]. In a separate case, a federal judge rebuked the hand‐picked ACIP panel as illegitimate, emphasizing that federal vaccine decisions must be grounded in science rather than ideology [8]. These judicial decisions underscore the extent to which federal vaccine governance has become both politicized and destabilized. At the same time, HHS has faced litigation for eliminating billions of dollars in infectious disease prevention grants, cuts that coincided with rising measles transmission. In 2025, multiple cities, counties, and labor unions sued HHS and Secretary Kennedy over the removal of $11 billion in outbreak‐prevention funding, arguing that the agency violated federal law and undermined national preparedness [9]. These disruptions have weakened the infrastructure that schools rely on to prevent and respond to vaccine‐preventable diseases. The consequences are visible across the country. Recent outbreaks have demonstrated how quickly measles spreads in undervaccinated communities and how easily cases move through shared public spaces, including schools. As vaccination norms erode, school districts face mounting challenges: protecting medically vulnerable students, managing exclusion policies during outbreaks, countering misinformation, and maintaining trust with families amid polarized political environments. In this context, evidence‐informed, school‐centered strategies are urgently needed. This commentary examines the personal, political, legal, and behavioral forces driving the measles epidemic and outlines evidence‐based, practical approaches schools can use to strengthen vaccination uptake, rebuild community trust, and safeguard student health. The assumption that most students are vaccinated, and therefore an unvaccinated student is safe, is becoming less of a guarantee. The health implications beyond the school campus are serious. Families must now take proactive steps to safeguard their health, as well as their fellow citizens. We cannot solely think of the school by itself; we must plan based on its connection to its community and how those communities are connected to each other in the real world. 1. Historical Context Since the 1980s, every state has required immunizations for schoolchildren to prevent outbreaks of diseases like measles, polio, and pertussis [10]. A recent study demonstrated these mandates, which include routine childhood vaccinations such as diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis vaccine; hepatitis B vaccine; varicella vaccine; oral and inactivated poliovirus vaccines; pneumococcal conjugate vaccine; measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine; hepatitis A vaccine; and rotavirus vaccine; prevented 508 million lifetime cases of illness, 32 million hospitalizations, and 1,129,000 deaths [11]. The financial savings were estimated at $540 billion in direct costs and $2.7 trillion in societal costs [11]. 2. Fear, Ideology, Access, and Vaccine Hesitancy The World Health Organization has identified vaccine hesitancy as one of the top 10 threats to global health [12]. Anti‐vaccine rhetoric has emboldened parents to keep their child(ren) from vaccination. From 2010 to 2024, nonmedical exemptions to childhood vaccine requirements in the United States increased 2.5%, with Florida exceeding 5% [13, 14]. This rise in exemption rates is a likely contributor to the resurgence of measles and subsequent epidemic. Parental concern regarding vaccine safety, overloading the immune system, and mistrust of healthcare authorities contributes to lowered vaccination rates in their children [15]. Researchers from the University of Pennsylvania surveyed more than 1500 adults regarding measles and 24% reported they believe the measles–mumps–rubella (MMR) vaccine causes autism [16]. Understanding why parents are less likely to have their children vaccinated requires looking at broader systems of fear, political identity, mistrust, and cultural values [17, 18]. Many parents observe the first signs of autism around the same age children receive the MMR vaccine. This temporal overlap makes the vaccine a psychologically convenient explanation for a deeply confusing or frightening diagnosis. Research shows that emotionally compelling personal stories often override scientific data [17]. Though a study published in the Lancet in 1998 reported a link between MMR and autism, it was later proven fraudulent and retracted [19]. However, it created a narrative that many parents still encounter today. The emotional simplicity of the story allows it to persist despite scientific rebuttals [20, 21]. Vaccine beliefs increasingly correlate not with scientific knowledge, but with political identity. The idea that “the government is hiding the truth” aligns well with anti‐establishment political narratives. Groups skeptical of federal authority often treat the MMR–autism myth as symbolic of broader government overreach. In political circles where individual liberty is a core value, vaccine skepticism is framed as protecting personal freedom, resisting state mandates, and defending parental authority over children [15, 16]. Surveys show that mistrust of vaccines correlates with broader skepticism toward public health recommendations in general. The MMR myth becomes not just a belief about science, but a cultural badge signaling adherence to values like autonomy and small‐government ideology [20, 21]. Lack of equitable healthcare access may heighten vaccine hesitancy and skepticism [22, 23]. When the medical system is experienced as untrustworthy or inaccessible, people are more likely to doubt its claims [24]. Parents facing long waits for diagnosis or limited support may look for alternative explanations. The myth provides one when systems fail them [25]. Many people struggle to distinguish between evidence‐based medical guidance and pseudoscientific content online [26]. The MMR–autism myth endures because it serves functions in people's psychological, social, and political lives, even though it does not hold up scientifically [27, 28]. 3. Promoting Childhood Vaccination in Schools and Communities Schools and their communities must implement practical, inclusive strategies for maintaining health and safety in schools, emphasizing the importance of access, contributing to stakeholder education and community‐driven solutions. Schools and their respective communities can administer vaccinations, even if they are not mandated by their state. In‐school or community vaccination clinics can occur, and education regarding all options and their potential strengths and limitations can be provided. 3.1. Strengthen Communication with Parents Parents are more likely to vaccinate their children when they receive clear, consistent, and positive information about vaccinations [29]. The CDC emphasizes that effective vaccine confidence efforts require practice‐wide messaging, ensuring everyone shares unified, accurate information about vaccine safety and schedules. Schools can reinforce this by sending home easy‐to‐read vaccine information in multiple languages, providing links to vetted, trustworthy resources, and including vaccination reminders in newsletters, websites, and parent portals [29]. These efforts help counter misinformation, one of the primary drivers of vaccine hesitancy. 3.2. Host Judgment‐Free Community Forums and Education Sessions Open, inclusive school‐community events can improve trust and provide space for parents to ask questions without fear of judgment. Community‐based engagement has been shown to reduce hesitancy by validating concerns and providing opportunities for honest discussion [30]. Effective forums should feature trusted messengers who can provide scientifically supported information that advocates for childhood vaccination, such as school nurses, pediatricians, and local health department representatives. Parents rely on healthcare providers' advice when making vaccination decisions. Schools can partner with local pediatricians, family physicians, or community clinics for these forums, invite nurses to speak during parent–teacher nights, and ensure that school health staff receive current training on vaccine communication [30]. These forums and sessions must emphasize listening, answering questions with clear evidence, and offer take‐home materials and follow‐up opportunities for one‐on‐one conversations. 3.3. Provide Accessible, Evidence‐Based Resources Educational materials should come from reputable, science‐based organizations. Museums, libraries, and community organizations use vetted toolkits, such as those compiled by Communities for Immunity, that provide sample messages, multilingual outreach tools, and resources tailored to specific populations [31]. Schools can incorporate these printed and online materials into health classes, parent meetings, school offices, and online platforms. Providing parents with credible information helps them feel confident in choosing on‐time vaccination [32]. Schools can also publish their vaccination rates so parents have access to information on the vaccination levels in their own schools and can make informed decisions regarding vaccinating their children and the risks of attending a particular school. 3.4. Promote Policies That Support On‐Time Immunization Strong institutional support also matters. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) strongly recommends routine, on‐time immunization for all children and adolescents because it is the safest and most effective way to prevent disease, disability, and death. Schools can reinforce this by reminding families of school‐entry vaccination requirements, clarifying which exemptions are allowed, and offering school‐based vaccination clinics in partnership with public health agencies [33]. Clear policies make expectations transparent and reduce logistical barriers. 4. Conclusions Infectious diseases do not discriminate based on belief systems or politics. They spread wherever susceptible individuals are present. As an epidemiologist, my aim is helping schools and their communities discern what best supports their health and well‐being, and how those choices can extend protection to families, friends, neighbors, and beyond. It is essential that schools and districts provide clear, evidence‐based education to all stakeholders. Every family deserves access to accurate information about vaccination and disease prevention. As vaccine mandates are either eliminated or made less stringent in several states, schools and their respective communities will face new challenges in protecting students, staff, and families from infectious diseases. For concerned families, faculty, and staff, vaccination remains the most effective and accessible preventive measure. Measles, hepatitis B, COVID‐19, and any other infectious diseases will not respect school boundaries. Protection must extend beyond the school campus to include immediate and extended family members, neighbors, and contacts across state and even country borders. School‐related events including but not limited to athletics, musical performances, plays, parent–teacher conferences, and field trips bring together individuals from inside and outside the school community. These settings facilitate the mixing of vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals, including those who may be immune‐compromised. The remaining hours off‐campus have many potential interactions that carry risk. Consider an unvaccinated student with their family and they are flying to visit relatives during a holiday. Do you know if the passenger next to you on the plane has received the measles vaccine? Would you ask them? Would you believe their answer? Rising numbers of unvaccinated students are a legitimate concern, even as families view vaccination as an individual right. Shifting mandates and uneven access may reinforce that sense of personal choice, but infectious diseases create risks that extend far beyond any one household. When individual decisions endanger medically vulnerable children or threaten school continuity, public health protections must take precedence. Schools and their communities remain essential in ensuring that protective measures are accessible, equitable, and evidence‐based. Local districts will increasingly translate public health guidance into practice. School health professionals must lead with clarity and compassion, helping families make informed decisions while reinforcing that collective safety depends on shared responsibility. In doing so, schools can respect autonomy without compromising the protection needed to keep students safe and learning. Funding The author has nothing to report. As vaccination norms erode, school districts face mounting challenges: protecting medically vulnerable students, managing exclusion policies during outbreaks, countering misinformation, and maintaining trust with families amid polarized political environments. In this context, evidence‐informed, school‐centered strategies are urgently needed. This commentary examines the personal, political, legal, and behavioral forces driving the measles epidemic and outlines evidence‐based, practical approaches schools can use to strengthen vaccination uptake, rebuild community trust, and safeguard student health. The assumption that most students are vaccinated, and therefore an unvaccinated student is safe, is becoming less of a guarantee. The health implications beyond the school campus are serious. Families must now take proactive steps to safeguard their health, as well as their fellow citizens. We cannot solely think of the school by itself; we must plan based on its connection to its community and how those communities are connected to each other in the real world. 1. Historical Context Since the 1980s, every state has required immunizations for schoolchildren to prevent outbreaks of diseases like measles, polio, and pertussis [10]. A recent study demonstrated these mandates, which include routine childhood vaccinations such as diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis vaccine; hepatitis B vaccine; varicella vaccine; oral and inactivated poliovirus vaccines; pneumococcal conjugate vaccine; measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine; hepatitis A vaccine; and rotavirus vaccine; prevented 508 million lifetime cases of illness, 32 million hospitalizations, and 1,129,000 deaths [11]. The financial savings were estimated at $540 billion in direct costs and $2.7 trillion in societal costs [11]. 2. Fear, Ideology, Access, and Vaccine Hesitancy The World Health Organization has identified vaccine hesitancy as one of the top 10 threats to global health [12]. Anti‐vaccine rhetoric has emboldened parents to keep their child(ren) from vaccination. From 2010 to 2024, nonmedical exemptions to childhood vaccine requirements in the United States increased 2.5%, with Florida exceeding 5% [13, 14]. This rise in exemption rates is a likely contributor to the resurgence of measles and subsequent epidemic. Parental concern regarding vaccine safety, overloading the immune system, and mistrust of healthcare authorities contributes to lowered vaccination rates in their children [15]. Researchers from the University of Pennsylvania surveyed more than 1500 adults regarding measles and 24% reported they believe the measles–mumps–rubella (MMR) vaccine causes autism [16]. Understanding why parents are less likely to have their children vaccinated requires looking at broader systems of fear, political identity, mistrust, and cultural values [17, 18]. Many parents observe the first signs of autism around the same age children receive the MMR vaccine. This temporal overlap makes the vaccine a psychologically convenient explanation for a deeply confusing or frightening diagnosis. Research shows that emotionally compelling personal stories often override scientific data [17]. Though a study published in the Lancet in 1998 reported a link between MMR and autism, it was later proven fraudulent and retracted [19]. However, it created a narrative that many parents still encounter today. The emotional simplicity of the story allows it to persist despite scientific rebuttals [20, 21]. Vaccine beliefs increasingly correlate not with scientific knowledge, but with political identity. The idea that “the government is hiding the truth” aligns well with anti‐establishment political narratives. Groups skeptical of federal authority often treat the MMR–autism myth as symbolic of broader government overreach. In political circles where individual liberty is a core value, vaccine skepticism is framed as protecting personal freedom, resisting state mandates, and defending parental authority over children [15, 16]. Surveys show that mistrust of vaccines correlates with broader skepticism toward public health recommendations in general. The MMR myth becomes not just a belief about science, but a cultural badge signaling adherence to values like autonomy and small‐government ideology [20, 21]. Lack of equitable healthcare access may heighten vaccine hesitancy and skepticism [22, 23]. When the medical system is experienced as untrustworthy or inaccessible, people are more likely to doubt its claims [24]. Parents facing long waits for diagnosis or limited support may look for alternative explanations. The myth provides one when systems fail them [25]. Many people struggle to distinguish between evidence‐based medical guidance and pseudoscientific content online [26]. The MMR–autism myth endures because it serves functions in people's psychological, social, and political lives, even though it does not hold up scientifically [27, 28]. 3. papers.title_original: Addressing the Measles Epidemic: Evidence Informed Approaches Schools Can Use to Promote Childhood Vaccination.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the re-emergence of measles as an epidemic threat in the United States, despite its elimination in 2000, and examines the role of schools in promoting childhood vaccination amid declining vaccination rates and policy changes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a narrative review focusing on the resurgence of measles in the United States from January 2025 to April 2026, with a particular emphasis on school-aged children and the impact of federal policy shifts.
analysis.methods: The analysis is based on a review of reported measles cases, federal court decisions, and policy changes, without generating or analyzing new datasets.
analysis.main_results: From January 2025 to April 2026, there were 4,102 diagnosed measles cases in the United States, with 92.5% of cases being unvaccinated or having unknown vaccination status; 23.7% of cases were in children under 5 years, and 47.4% in those aged 5–19.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the resurgence as a consequence of declining vaccination rates, politicization of immunization policy, and erosion of institutional authority, with federal policy shifts exacerbating the epidemic.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for schools to implement evidence-informed strategies to promote vaccination, protect vulnerable students, manage outbreaks, and counter misinformation in polarized environments.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on reported cases and policy analyses without primary data collection or controlled experiments, and the narrative review approach may introduce bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the re-emergence of measles in the United States, which was declared eliminated in 2000 but has resurged as an epidemic threat. From January 2025 to April 2026, 4,102 cases were reported, with 92.5% unvaccinated or of unknown status, disproportionately affecting children under 5 (23.7%) and those aged 5–19 (47.4%). The resurgence is attributed to declining vaccination rates, politicization of immunization policy, and federal policy shifts, including attempts to reduce recommended childhood vaccines and cut infectious disease prevention funding. Federal courts have intervened to block these changes, citing their potential to harm public health. Schools, now at the epicenter of the outbreak, face challenges in protecting vulnerable students, managing exclusion policies, and countering misinformation. The study underscores the need for evidence-informed strategies to promote vaccination and maintain public trust.

papers.title: Changing epidemiology and transmission dynamics of measles in Ho Chi Minh City: a comparison of the 2018–2020 and 2024–2025 outbreaks
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Measles remains a major public health threat worldwide. Following a resurgence of cases, Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC) experienced a severe outbreak in 2024–2025 that differed from the 2018–2020 epidemic. We compared the epidemiology and transmission dynamics of these two outbreaks to inform future surveillance and vaccination strategies. Methods Line-list data for measles cases reported in HCMC between 2018 and 2025 were extracted from the infectious disease surveillance system. Demographic changes were assessed using cross-sectional age distributions and longitudinal birth-cohort analyses. Transmission dynamics were characterized by estimating the effective reproduction number (Rt) using the Cori and Wallinga– Teunis methods. Age-stratified Who-Infected-Whom transmission matrices were constructed to quantify within- and between-age-group transmission before and after interventions. Results The 2018–2020 outbreak primarily affected children under five years of age (median age 3.75 years, IQR 0.9–9.1), whereas the 2024–2025 outbreak shifted toward older age groups (median age 8.4 years, IQR 1–14). Birth-cohort analyses identified two major immunity gaps: children born during the COVID-19 immunization disruption (2019–2023) and adolescents and young adults born before 2014 who were not eligible for the 2018 outbreak response immunization campaign. The 2024–2025 outbreak also showed broader spatial spread and a reversed geographic trajectory compared with the earlier epidemic. Transmission patterns changed substantially, with the 2018– 2020 outbreak sustained mainly by transmission among young children, whereas the 2024–2025 outbreak was driven by older age groups, with individuals >15 years acting as an important source of infection for infants. Conclusion The epidemiology of measles in HCMC has shifted from predominantly pediatric transmission to increasing involvement of adolescents and adults, reflecting accumulated immunity gaps across multiple birth cohorts. These findings suggest that age-restricted outbreak response immunization may leave residual susceptible populations that contribute to future outbreaks. Achieving sustainable measles elimination will require vaccination strategies that address historical immunity gaps across all vulnerable age groups, in addition to maintaining high routine childhood vaccination coverage.

papers.title: Risk-targeted interventions for measles control-Lessons from an emergency response project in the Katanga Region, Democratic Republic of the Congo (2021-2023)
papers.abstract: Abstract The Urgepi project is a measles emergency initiative implemented by Médecins Sans Frontières Operational Centre Paris (MSF-OCP) in the Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of Congo, a setting characterized by recurrent measles epidemics with substantial public health impact. To maximize impact, the project employs a risk-targeted approach directing resources to selected health zones to strengthen surveillance, implement preventive vaccination, and ensure timely epidemic response. This study presents the Urgepi approach, and, based on surveillance data from 2021-2023, evaluates the effectiveness of targeted preventive activities, explores strategies for prioritizing interventions amid multiple alerts, and assesses the overall impact of interventions on measles epidemics. Preventive vaccination successfully averted epidemics in six of the nine vaccinated high-risk health zones, while nine of ten non-vaccinated priority health zones experienced large epidemics. In the three vaccinated health zones that experienced epidemics, more locally adapted vaccination strategies would have been required to achieve higher coverage. Regarding the project’s approach to prioritize alerts for investigations and interventions, we found that the Urgepi alert prioritization score was positively associated with subsequent epidemic size, suggesting that this approach allowed effective and timely targeting of larger local measles epidemics. Although no clear impact of epidemic response vaccination on case numbers was observed, likely due to biases introduced in case reporting through provision of free case management, a 50% reduction in the median epidemic duration was recorded. In conclusion, the findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the Urgepi project’s risk-targeted approach for measles prevention and control and highlight the importance of timely and context-specific interventions. Key questions What is already known on this topic – Measles can, in theory, be effectively controlled through preventive vaccination or rapid immunization responses during outbreaks. However, many countries continue to face significant operational challenges. What this study adds – We demonstrate how a risk-targeted approach, with prioritization of both preventive and response actions, can optimize resources in the fight against measles. How this study might affect research, practice or policy – Similar risk-targeted approaches can help national programs prioritize geographic areas for measles prevention and outbreak response when it is not feasible to cover all regions due to operational constraints.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 Urgepi 项目是无国界医生组织巴黎行动中心 (MSF-OCP) 在刚果民主共和国加丹加地区实施的一项 麻疹 紧急举措,该地区经常出现 麻疹 流行病,对公共卫生造成重大影响。为了最大限度地发挥影响,该项目采用以风险为目标的方法,将资源引导到选定的卫生区,以加强监测,实施预防性疫苗接种,并确保及时应对疫情。本研究提出了Urgepi方法,并基于2021-2023年麻疹数据,评估有针对性的预防活动的有效性,探索在多个警报中优先干预的策略,并评估干预措施对麻疹流行病的总体影响。预防性疫苗接种在9个接种疫苗的高风险卫生区中的6个成功避免了流行病,而10个未接种疫苗的重点卫生区中的9个出现了大规模流行病。在经历过流行病的三个疫苗接种卫生区,需要采取更适合当地的 疫苗接种 策略才能实现更高的覆盖率。关于该项目确定调查和干预警报优先级的方法,我们发现 Urgepi 警报优先级评分与随后的流行病规模呈正相关,这表明这种方法可以有效、及时地针对较大的当地 麻疹 流行病。尽管没有观察到流行病应对 疫苗接种 对病例数的明显影响,可能是由于通过提供免费病例管理在病例报告中引入了偏差,但流行病持续时间中位数减少了 50%。总之,研究结果证明了 Urgepi 项目针对 麻疹 预防和控制的风险针对性方法的有效性,并强调了及时和针对具体情况的干预措施的重要性。关键问题 关于该主题的已知信息 – 理论上,可以通过预防性 麻疹 或 麻疹 期间的快速免疫反应来有效控制 麻疹。然而,许多国家继续面临重大的运营挑战。这项研究的补充内容——我们展示了以风险为目标的方法,并优先考虑预防和响应行动,可以在对抗 麻疹 的斗争中优化资源。这项研究可能如何影响研究、实践或政策——当由于操作限制而无法覆盖所有地区时,类似的风险目标方法可以帮助国家计划优先考虑 麻疹 预防和 麻疹 应对的地理区域。

papers.title: Investigating the Trifecta of Measles Cases, Vaccination Rates, and Homeschooling in the United States
papers.abstract: The resurgence in measles cases in the United States over the past couple of years has sparked concern among the populace in the sphere of increased hospitalizations and mortality rates despite the availability of a well tolerated and effective vaccine. Measles is a highly contagious viral disease which is spread through the air via aerosols and respiratory droplets and primarily affects younger individuals. A study was done to assess the effect of homeschooling and vaccination rates on Measles cases employing statistical tests multiple regression and Pearson correlation coefficient. Independent variables comprised MMR average vaccination rates from 2015 to 2025, and homeschooling data from 2024. Regression analysis revealed homeschooling had a significant effect on the number of measles cases (P=.004) with a positive correlation (r=0.4, P=0.01). The vaccination rate variable was not found to be statistically significant, however the correlation coefficient was positive (r=0.06, P>0.05). These findings add to the current body of knowledge as researchers continue to explore causes for the recent spike in measles cases in the United States.

papers.title: Measles and Rubella Elimination Trends in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region, 2023–2024: Progress and Recent Epidemiological Shifts
papers.abstract: Background: Measles and rubella remain key indicators of immunization system performance and are central to the Immunization Agenda 2030 (IA2030). Disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic have widened immunity gaps and accelerated resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases across multiple regions. This study assesses progress toward measles and rubella elimination in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) during 2023–2024. Methods: We conducted a retrospective descriptive analysis of measles and rubella surveillance data, WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC), and Joint Reporting Form (eJRF) data for all 22 EMR countries and territories. Key indicators included disease incidence, MCV1 and MCV2 coverage, surveillance performance metrics, and verified elimination status. Results: Regional measles incidence increased from 110.8 to 116.3 per million population, while rubella incidence more than doubled from 1.9 to 4.3 per million. Large outbreaks in Yemen, Iraq, and Afghanistan disproportionally drove regional trends. MCV1 coverage remained stable at approximately 80%, while MCV2 coverage increased marginally from 73% to 75%. Only nine of 22 countries achieved ≥95% coverage for both doses in 2024. Persistent zero-dose populations, high dropout rates, and ongoing immunity gaps sustained transmission across multiple settings. Conclusions: The EMR remains off track to achieve measles and rubella elimination by 2030. Accelerated, equity-focused efforts are urgently needed to strengthen routine immunization systems, reduce zero-dose population, enhance surveillance capacity, and improve outbreak response—particularly in fragile and conflicted-affected settings.

Disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic have widened immunity gaps and accelerated resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases across multiple regions. This study assesses progress toward measles and rubella elimination in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) during 2023–2024. Methods: We conducted a retrospective descriptive analysis of measles and rubella surveillance data, WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC), and Joint Reporting Form (eJRF) data for all 22 EMR countries and territories. Key indicators included disease incidence, MCV1 and MCV2 coverage, surveillance performance metrics, and verified elimination status. Results: Regional measles incidence increased from 110.8 to 116.3 per million population, while rubella incidence more than doubled from 1.9 to 4.3 per million. Large outbreaks in Yemen, Iraq, and Afghanistan disproportionally drove regional trends. MCV1 coverage remained stable at approximately 80%, while MCV2 coverage increased marginally from 73% to 75%. Only nine of 22 countries achieved ≥95% coverage for both doses in 2024. Persistent zero-dose populations, high dropout rates, and ongoing immunity gaps sustained transmission across multiple settings. Conclusions: The EMR remains off track to achieve measles and rubella elimination by 2030. Accelerated, equity-focused efforts are urgently needed to strengthen routine immunization systems, reduce zero-dose population, enhance surveillance capacity, and improve outbreak response—particularly in fragile and conflicted-affected settings.

papers.title: Investigation of measles outbreak in Pakistan (2022 to 2023): Exploring comorbidities, complications, and molecular characterization
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Measles remains a major public health concern worldwide, particularly in regions with insufficient vaccination coverage and healthcare infrastructure, like Pakistan. The purpose of this study is to investigate the epidemiological, molecular, and phylogenetic characteristics of the measles outbreak in Pakistan during 2022-2023 and highlight the areas of improvement that can contribute to the better understanding of the disease and inform strategies for effective outbreak management and vaccination optimization. METHODS Throat swabs were collected from patients (n = 183) admitted at PIMS, Islamabad, Pakistan, from December 2022- December 2023. Statistical analysis of data was conducted on SPSS-21 software. The phylogenetics, amino acid substitutions, their functional analysis, and structural analysis of partial nucleoprotein were performed by using different bioinformatics software. RESULTS Most of the measles patients were infants with a high prevalence of comorbidity and complications, and significant number of patients had inadequate vaccination coverage. The phylogenetic analysis revealed relatedness to B3 strains circulating in Russia and the USA, emphasizing the global spread. The amino acid substitutions and structure analysis highlighted minor structural variations in current isolates as compared to the reference strain. CONCLUSION The findings underscore the importance of continuous surveillance and understanding of measles epidemiology and viral variations for effective outbreak management and vaccination optimization, ultimately aiming to mitigate the morbidity and mortality associated with measles outbreaks in Pakistan and similar settings globally. This study exemplifies the significance of interdisciplinary collaboration in confronting complex infectious disease challenges, emphasizing the imperative of continuous monitoring and preparedness in combating measles through vaccination.

papers.title_zh: 巴基斯坦 麻疹 暴发 的调查(2022 年至 2023 年):探索合并症、并发症和分子特征
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND Measles remains a major public health concern worldwide, particularly in regions with insufficient vaccination coverage and healthcare infrastructure, like Pakistan. The purpose of this study is to investigate the epidemiological, molecular, and phylogenetic characteristics of the measles outbreak in Pakistan during 2022-2023 and highlight the areas of improvement that can contribute to the better understanding of the disease and inform strategies for effective outbreak management and vaccination optimization. METHODS Throat swabs were collected from patients (n = 183) admitted at PIMS, Islamabad, Pakistan, from December 2022- December 2023. Statistical analysis of data was conducted on SPSS-21 software. The phylogenetics, amino acid substitutions, their functional analysis, and structural analysis of partial nucleoprotein were performed by using different bioinformatics software. RESULTS Most of the measles patients were infants with a high prevalence of comorbidity and complications, and significant number of patients had inadequate vaccination coverage. The phylogenetic analysis revealed relatedness to B3 strains circulating in Russia and the USA, emphasizing the global spread. The amino acid substitutions and structure analysis highlighted minor structural variations in current isolates as compared to the reference strain. CONCLUSION The findings underscore the importance of continuous surveillance and understanding of measles epidemiology and viral variations for effective outbreak management and vaccination optimization, ultimately aiming to mitigate the morbidity and mortality associated with measles outbreaks in Pakistan and similar settings globally. This study exemplifies the significance of interdisciplinary collaboration in confronting complex infectious disease challenges, emphasizing the imperative of continuous monitoring and preparedness in combating measles through vaccination.

papers.title: Seroprevalence of measles-specific IgM and IgG antibodies among children (0–12 years) with measles-like symptoms: a hospital-based cross-sectional study in Northeast Nigeria
papers.abstract: Nigeria has one of the highest measles burdens and the lowest vaccination coverage worldwide. The WHO AFRO region, including Nigeria, is currently working towards a revised target of eliminating measles by 2030. Nigeria’s strategy includes improving MCV1 coverage at 9 months, supplemental immunization for children aged 9–59 months, and intensified case-based surveillance. Recently, MCV2 was introduced and is being piloted. Achieving at least 95% coverage with MCV2 at 15 months is essential for herd immunity. Despite these efforts, measles outbreaks persist, worsened by armed conflicts and the COVID-19 pandemic in Northeast Nigeria which disrupts health infrastructures and ultimately affects immunization activities. This study evaluates serological patterns and confirms measles infection among symptomatic children attending healthcare facilities in Northeast Nigeria. By integrating serology with socio-demographic and clinical risk factors, we seek to evaluate the serological profile and identify proportion of susceptible individuals among symptomatic children in some selected clinical settings in Northeast Nigeria. Children with clinically suspected measles cases were recruited from selected primary healthcare centres (PHC) in Yobe, Borno and Adamawa between November 2022-July 2023. The study analysed serum samples for measles-specific IgM antibodies ( n = 558) and measles-specific IgG antibodies ( n = 372). IgM antibodies were determined using the EUROIMMUN measles virus IgM ELISA kit, and IgG antibodies were determined using the Calbiotech measles IgG kit. Odds Ratio (OR) and 95% Confidence Intervals (CI) were calculated from 2 × 2 tables using a Univariate Logistic Regression model. The association between measles and socio-demographic and risk factors was analysed using chi-square. Statistical significance was set at P ≤ 0.05. In this study, seroprevalence was defined by the presence of IgM to indicate recent infection and IgG to indicate past exposure or immunity. The results showed a seroprevalence of 29.2% for measles IgM and 32.8% for measles IgG. Measles IgM and IgG antibodies were detected more among males compared to females, with a seroprevalence of 30.6% and 33.3% respectively. No significant association was observed between sex and Measles virus seropositivity for either IgM or IgG ( P > 0.05). Although the odds ratio for males was 1.23, the 95% confidence interval (0.82–1.82) indicated that this difference was not statistically significant. The highest IgM and IgG antibodies were observed amongst children aged 1–3 years with a prevalence of 40.8% and 46.5% respectively. Vaccination was associated with a significant reduction in the odds of measles infection (OR 0.30; 95% CI, 0.20–0.44; P ≤ 0.005). This study is limited by potential selection and recall biases. By focusing exclusively on children presenting with measles-like symptoms, the findings are not representative of the general paediatric population. Furthermore, reliance on parental recall for vaccination history introduces a high likelihood of information bias. Our study identifies a high frequency of measles seropositivity among symptomatic children in selected healthcare facilities in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe states. While this study highlights a high prevalence of non-vaccination among symptomatic children, further research should focus on the need for localised investigation into immunization history in symptomatic cases.

papers.title_zh: 具有 麻疹 样症状的儿童(0-12 岁)中 麻疹 特异性 IgM 和 IgG 抗体的 血清流行率:尼日利亚东北部医院的横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: Nigeria has one of the highest measles burdens and the lowest vaccination coverage worldwide. The WHO AFRO region, including Nigeria, is currently working towards a revised target of eliminating measles by 2030. Nigeria’s strategy includes improving MCV1 coverage at 9 months, supplemental immunization for children aged 9–59 months, and intensified case-based surveillance. Recently, MCV2 was introduced and is being piloted. Achieving at least 95% coverage with MCV2 at 15 months is essential for herd immunity. Despite these efforts, measles outbreaks persist, worsened by armed conflicts and the COVID-19 pandemic in Northeast Nigeria which disrupts health infrastructures and ultimately affects immunization activities. This study evaluates serological patterns and confirms measles infection among symptomatic children attending healthcare facilities in Northeast Nigeria. By integrating serology with socio-demographic and clinical risk factors, we seek to evaluate the serological profile and identify proportion of susceptible individuals among symptomatic children in some selected clinical settings in Northeast Nigeria. Children with clinically suspected measles cases were recruited from selected primary healthcare centres (PHC) in Yobe, Borno and Adamawa between November 2022-July 2023. The study analysed serum samples for measles-specific IgM antibodies ( n = 558) and measles-specific IgG antibodies ( n = 372). IgM antibodies were determined using the EUROIMMUN measles virus IgM ELISA kit, and IgG antibodies were determined using the Calbiotech measles IgG kit. Odds Ratio (OR) and 95% Confidence Intervals (CI) were calculated from 2 × 2 tables using a Univariate Logistic Regression model. The association between measles and socio-demographic and risk factors was analysed using chi-square. Statistical significance was set at P ≤ 0.05. In this study, seroprevalence was defined by the presence of IgM to indicate recent infection and IgG to indicate past exposure or immunity. The results showed a seroprevalence of 29.2% for measles IgM and 32.8% for measles IgG. Measles IgM and IgG antibodies were detected more among males compared to females, with a seroprevalence of 30.6% and 33.3% respectively. No significant association was observed between sex and Measles virus seropositivity for either IgM or IgG ( P > 0.05). Although the odds ratio for males was 1.23, the 95% confidence interval (0.82–1.82) indicated that this difference was not statistically significant. The highest IgM and IgG antibodies were observed amongst children aged 1–3 years with a prevalence of 40.8% and 46.5% respectively. Vaccination was associated with a significant reduction in the odds of measles infection (OR 0.30; 95% CI, 0.20–0.44; P ≤ 0.005). This study is limited by potential selection and recall biases. By focusing exclusively on children presenting with measles-like symptoms, the findings are not representative of the general paediatric population. Furthermore, reliance on parental recall for vaccination history introduces a high likelihood of information bias. Our study identifies a high frequency of measles seropositivity among symptomatic children in selected healthcare facilities in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe states. While this study highlights a high prevalence of non-vaccination among symptomatic children, further research should focus on the need for localised investigation into immunization history in symptomatic cases.

papers.title: Evaluation of measles and acute flaccid paralysis surveillance systems in Southern Province, Zambia, 2022 - 2024
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: The Vaccine-Preventable Disease (VPD) surveillance system in Zambia integrates routine immunization monitoring with disease surveillance to guide control measures. In 2022, Zambia recorded 422 measles cases and 37 deaths, with Southern Province recording the highest case fatality rate (11.2%), suggesting possible weaknesses in surveillance performance and outbreak response systems. This evaluation assessed the measles and acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) surveillance systems in Southern province of Zambia from 2022 to 2024. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional surveillance system evaluation following the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidelines. We purposively selected three districts and three facilities from each district, based on measles and AFP case burden and vaccination coverage. We collected data on system’s simplicity, usefulness, and acceptability from 27 participants using structured questionnaires. We also collected data from the electronic Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (eIDSR) system and World Health Organization databases to assess, data completeness, timeliness, and accuracy. Results were summarized using frequencies and percentages. Results: The measles and AFP surveillance systems comprised both passive and active surveillance operating across community, health facility, district, and provincial levels. The systems demonstrated high levels of simplicity (mean score: 84.6%), usefulness (90.5%), and acceptability (90.8%). However, surveillance performance was limited by suboptimal data quality, with mean completeness of 66.7%, timeliness of 51.1%, and data accuracy of 50%. We also identified key operational challenges of inadequate specimen transportation and insufficient program funding. Conclusion: The measles and AFP surveillance systems in Southern Province are functional, simple, acceptable, and well-integrated into routine services. However, significant gaps in data quality limit their effectiveness for early outbreak detection and timely public health response. Strengthening data management, specimen transport, and sustainable program financing will be critical to improving surveillance performance and accelerating progress toward vaccine-preventable disease control and elimination targets. Keywords: Acute Flaccid Paralysis (AFP), measles, surveillance systems, vaccine-preventable disease, Zambia.

papers.title: Preliminary safety data from a randomised trial of early versus standard timing of administration of measles-rubella vaccine in Ugandan infants
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Measles remains a major cause of child morbidity and mortality in low-resource settings. Young infants are particularly at risk of severe disease, with many lacking protective levels of maternal antibodies by six months. Vaccination before nine months in high-burden settings may confer earlier protection; however, concerns exist about its effectiveness at this age. We present early findings on enrolment, safety, and measles infections following the administration of a registered measles-containing vaccine at six months versus nine months (MR1) with a subsequent booster (MR2) at 12 or 18 months of age. Methods We conducted an open-label randomised controlled non-inferiority trial at four health facilities in Kampala, Uganda. Infants aged 24–28 weeks were randomly assigned to receive MR at six and 12 months (group A), nine and 18 months (group B) or six and 18 months (group C). Infants were electronically randomised in a 1:1:1 ratio using block randomisation of varying sizes, stratified by site, maternal HIV status and baseline haemoglobin level. Caretakers recorded solicited reactions on paper diary cards, with safety-related events evaluated. Findings 450 infants received MR1 and were enrolled. No differences in local or systemic post-vaccination events between the six and nine months MR1 groups were observed [Local: 21·2% versus 21·9% ( p = 0·959), systemic: 29·2% vs. 27·7% ( p = 0·845)]. Most local reactions were mild and within the first four days. The majority (5/6) of hospitalisations followed common childhood illnesses, with one non-vaccine-related death six months post-MR1. Sixteen laboratory-confirmed cases of measles (10) and rubella (6), and three clinical measles cases before MR1 were registered. Most measles cases (70·0%) occurred in group C, with no measles cases registered two weeks post-MR2. Conclusion We provide further evidence on the safety of administering a measles-containing vaccine at six months of age. Trial registration : The trial was registered on 31st October 2024 with Clinicaltrials.gov with the identifier NCT06667206.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 麻疹 仍然是资源匮乏地区儿童发病和 死亡率 的主要原因。年幼的婴儿尤其面临严重疾病的风险,许多婴儿在六个月时缺乏保护性母体抗体水平。在高负担环境中九个月前使用 疫苗接种 可能会提供更早的保护;然而,人们对其在这个年龄段的有效性存在担忧。我们提出了有关注册、安全性和 麻疹 感染的早期研究结果,这些结果是在 6 个月龄与 9 个月龄(MR1)给予注册的含有 麻疹 的 麻疹 以及随后在 12 或 18 个月龄时进行加强注射(MR2)后的结果。方法 我们在乌干达坎帕拉的四个卫生机构进行了一项开放标签随机对照非劣效性试验。24-28 周的婴儿被随机分配在 6 个月和 12 个月(A 组)、9 个月和 18 个月(B 组)或 6 个月和 18 个月(C 组)时接受 MR。使用不同规模的分组随机化,按地点、母亲艾滋病毒状况和基线血红蛋白水平分层,以 1:1:1 的比例对婴儿进行电子随机化。看护人员将请求的反应记录在纸质日记卡上,并对安全相关事件进行评估。结果 450 名婴儿接受了 MR1 并被登记。在 6 个月和 9 个月的 MR1 组之间,未观察到 疫苗接种 后局部或全身事件的差异 [局部:21·2% 与 21·9% (p = 0·959),全身:29·2% 与 27·7% (p = 0·845)]。大多数局部反应都是轻微的,并且发生在最初的四天内。大多数 (5/6) 的住院治疗是因为常见的儿童疾病,其中 1 例与 疫苗 无关的死亡发生在 MR1 后六个月。登记了 16 例实验室确诊的 麻疹 病例(10 例)和风疹病例(6 例),以及 MR1 之前的 3 例临床 麻疹 病例。大多数 麻疹 病例 (70·0%) 发生在 C 组,MR2 后两周没有登记 麻疹 病例。结论 我们提供了关于在六个月大时给予含有 麻疹 的 疫苗 的安全性的进一步证据。试验注册:该试验于 2024 年 10 月 31 日在 ClinicalTrials.gov 注册,标识符为 NCT06667206。

papers.title: Distinct Humoral Response Development to Measles Virus across Vaccine Platforms 2251461
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction As measles incidences increase globally, it is imperative to elucidate the features of a protective humoral response. Methods In this study, a phage-display immunoprecipitation sequencing technology, VirScan, was employed to evaluate viral epitope coverage by antibodies raised to infection of rhesus macaques with wild-type (WT) measles virus (MeV), or after vaccination with a live-attenuated MeV vaccine (LAMV), the triple measles mumps rubella vaccine (MMR) or a novel recombinant MeV hemagglutinin protein-based vaccine (rMeVH). Vaccinated animals were also challenged with WT MeV to measure antibody epitope reactivity during a recall. Results The results demonstrate that WT MeV infection elicited antibodies with a broader epitope reactivity profile than LAMV-containing vaccines. The rMeVH vaccine not only resulted in a narrow H-protein specific antibody profile, but induced specificities that were distinct from those induced to WT MeV or LAMV. All vaccinated animals expanded the breadth of their MeV-specific antibody binding repertoires following WT MeV challenge. The MeV-specific VarScore, a measure of overall antigen-binding, was positively correlated with total IgG titers assessed by ELISA, avidity, and neutralizing titer. Conclusion These results demonstrate the large effects of vaccination platforms on the breadth and fine-specificity of anti-measles induced humoral responses. Funding Source NIH Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

analysis.research_question_and_background: As measles incidences increase globally, it is imperative to elucidate the features of a protective humoral response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this study, rhesus macaques were infected with wild-type measles virus or vaccinated with a live-attenuated measles vaccine, the triple measles mumps rubella vaccine, or a novel recombinant measles hemagglutinin protein-based vaccine.
analysis.methods: Phage-display immunoprecipitation sequencing technology (VirScan) was employed to evaluate viral epitope coverage by antibodies, and vaccinated animals were challenged with wild-type measles virus to measure antibody epitope reactivity during a recall.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results demonstrate the large effects of vaccination platforms on the breadth and fine-specificity of anti-measles induced humoral responses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the humoral response to measles virus across different vaccine platforms in rhesus macaques. Using VirScan technology, the researchers found that wild-type measles virus infection elicited broader antibody epitope reactivity compared to live-attenuated vaccines. The MeV-specific VarScore correlated with IgG titers, avidity, and neutralizing titers. These results demonstrate significant platform-dependent effects on antibody responses, informing future vaccine design strategies.

papers.title_original: Hematologic Changes Associated With Measles Infection: A Retrospective Chart Review.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines hematologic changes associated with measles virus infection in humans, focusing on the pathogen Measles morbillivirus (Morbillivirus hominis), the disease measles, and its severe complication subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. The central question addresses the hematologic manifestations and laboratory abnormalities observed during measles infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base consists of a retrospective chart review study design analyzing hematologic parameters in measles-infected patients. The review method includes retrospective chart extraction and analysis of laboratory data from clinical records, with no explicit mention of systematic search strategies, eligibility criteria beyond measles diagnosis, or meta-analytic processes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identifies consistent hematologic abnormalities associated with measles infection, including lymphopenia and thrombocytopenia, as key findings supported by retrospective clinical data. These changes are highlighted as characteristic laboratory features during acute measles episodes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes limited data on long-term hematologic recovery post-measles infection and the absence of standardized protocols for hematologic monitoring in measles cases. There is also a lack of comparative data across different measles genotypes (e.g., B3, D8) regarding hematologic severity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for prospective studies to validate hematologic markers as prognostic indicators in measles and to establish standardized laboratory monitoring guidelines for infected patients. Additionally, it suggests investigating genotype-specific hematologic differences to refine clinical management.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence from a retrospective chart review on hematologic changes during measles virus infection in humans. It identifies consistent findings of lymphopenia and thrombocytopenia as characteristic laboratory abnormalities in acute measles episodes. The evidence base relies on retrospective clinical data extraction without systematic search methods or meta-analysis. Key gaps include limited data on long-term recovery and genotype-specific differences, while standardized monitoring protocols remain undeveloped. The review prioritizes prospective validation of hematologic markers for prognosis and the establishment of clinical monitoring guidelines to improve patient management.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了与人类 麻疹病毒 感染相关的血液学变化,重点关注病原体 麻疹 麻疹病毒(人麻疹病毒)、疾病 麻疹 及其严重并发症 亚急性硬化性全脑炎。中心问题涉及 麻疹 感染期间观察到的血液学表现和实验室异常。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 证据基础包括回顾性图表审查研究设计,分析 麻疹 感染患者的血液学参数。审查方法包括从临床记录中提取和分析实验室数据的回顾性图表,没有明确提及系统搜索策略、麻疹 诊断 之外的资格标准或荟萃分析过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述确定了与 麻疹 感染相关的一致血液学异常,包括淋巴细胞减少和血小板减少,作为回顾性临床数据支持的关键发现。这些变化被强调为急性 麻疹 发作期间的典型实验室特征。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出,关于 麻疹 感染后长期血液学恢复的数据有限,并且缺乏 麻疹 病例血液学监测的标准化方案。不同 麻疹 基因型(例如 B3、D8)之间也缺乏关于血液学严重程度的比较数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要进行前瞻性研究来验证血液学标志物作为 麻疹 的预后指标,并为感染患者建立标准化的实验室监测指南。此外,它建议调查基因型特异性血液学差异以完善临床管理。

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study was needed to address geographic variation in measles vaccine coverage among children aged 7 years in Northern California, as measles remains a significant public health concern due to its high transmissibility and potential for outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study was conducted in Northern California, focusing on children aged 7 years across various county census tracts to assess measles-containing vaccine coverage at the local level.
analysis.methods: The study utilized a cohort design, analyzing data from children aged 7 years in Northern California to evaluate measles vaccine coverage at the county census tract level.
analysis.main_results: The study found significant geographic variation in measles vaccine coverage among children aged 7 years in Northern California, with some census tracts reporting lower coverage rates than others.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as highlighting disparities in vaccine coverage that may contribute to localized measles outbreaks, offering a novel perspective on the importance of geographic analysis in public health planning.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted public health interventions to improve measles vaccine coverage in underserved areas, potentially reducing the risk of outbreaks and enhancing disease control strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on existing data and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to its large geographic scope and detailed census tract-level analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines geographic variation in measles vaccine coverage among children aged 7 years in Northern California. It highlights disparities in immunization rates across different census tracts, which may contribute to localized outbreaks. The findings suggest that targeted public health interventions are necessary to address these gaps. The study is a cohort analysis, providing strong evidence for the importance of geographic data in vaccine planning. However, it is limited by the use of existing data and potential confounding factors. The results emphasize the need for improved surveillance and tailored strategies to enhance measles control in specific communities.

papers.abstract_zh: 这项 队列研究 研究评估了北加州 7 岁儿童在县人口普查区水平上包含 麻疹 的 疫苗 覆盖率的变化。
papers.summary_zh: 这项 队列研究 研究评估了北加州 7 岁儿童在县人口普查区水平上包含 麻疹 的 疫苗 覆盖率的变化。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究需要解决北加州 7 岁儿童中 麻疹 疫苗 覆盖率的地理差异,因为 麻疹 由于其高传播性和 暴发 的潜力,仍然是一个重大的公共卫生问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项 队列研究 研究在北加州进行,重点关注各个县人口普查区的 7 岁儿童,以评估当地层面包含 麻疹 的 疫苗 覆盖范围。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究采用 队列研究 设计,分析北加州 7 岁儿童的数据,以评估县人口普查区层面的 麻疹 疫苗 覆盖率。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,北加州 7 岁儿童的 麻疹 疫苗 覆盖率存在显着的地理差异,一些人口普查区报告的覆盖率低于其他人口普查区。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了 疫苗 覆盖范围的差异,这可能有助于本地化 麻疹 暴发,为地理分析在公共卫生规划中的重要性提供了一个新颖的视角。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为有针对性的公共卫生干预措施提供信息,以提高服务不足地区的 麻疹 疫苗 覆盖率,从而有可能降低 麻疹 的风险并增强疾病控制策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对现有数据的依赖以及可能存在未测量的混杂因素而受到限制,但由于其广阔的地理范围和详细的人口普查区域水平分析,证据是强有力的。

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for measles surveillance and immunisation catch-up programs, particularly in regions affected by pandemic-related service disruptions. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on measles immunisation services in Indonesia, focusing on the period from 2018 to 2024. It highlights how disruptions during the pandemic may have created immunisation debt, potentially leading to measles resurgence. The research uses longitudinal ecological data from 34–38 provinces, divided into pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic phases, to examine measles outbreak frequency and MR1 vaccination coverage. The results show significant differences in KLB frequency across these phases, suggesting a link between pandemic-related service disruptions and measles resurgence. The authors interpret these findings as evidence of the need for targeted immunisation catch-up programs to mitigate the risk of outbreaks. The study's ecological design limits its ability to establish causal relationships, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the reliance on aggregated data. These findings have important implications for public health planning and measles control strategies in Indonesia and other regions with similar challenges.

papers.title: Measles Prediction Modeling using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)
papers.abstract: Measles, a viral and communicable illness with life-threatening complications, begins with an 8-12-day incubation period accompanied by fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis. The Measles Virus (MeV) enters the alveolar macrophages of the host or its dendritic cells, replicates, and then spreads to the surrounding surfaces. As a result, we focus on the use of Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) for the prediction of measles. The models (ANFIS and ANN) were employed and evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R2), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Pearson correlation coefficient (R), and Percentage Bias (PBIAS) as evaluation metrics. The results showed that ANFIS, ANN, and MLR showed R values of 0.9810, 0.9960, and 0.9750 for both training and test. Remarkably, ANN scored lower in terms of the RMSE metric with values of 0.6790 and 0.6809 for both training and testing. In addition, the ANN PBIAS values were 0.1080 and 0.1142 for both training and testing, respectively. In conclusion, ANFIS and ANN have demonstrated effectiveness in modeling measles occurrences, thus, as a valuable tool for public health and decision makers, especially in determining strategies that will enhance public safety.
